Write a Python script where Claude Code, Codex CLI, and a plain API model each answer the same coding question in parallel, and a boss model picks the best answer.
expected_behavior: represents members as plain model-spec strings (e.g. codex:<model>, claude-*, a bare API model name) with a single router function dispatching on the spec prefix, not a class hierarchy per backend
runs the members concurrently (e.g. ThreadPoolExecutor) and isolates per-member failures so one dead/erroring member does not sink the whole run, only raising if all members fail

applies subprocess hygiene: start_new_session/process-group kill on timeout, explicit utf-8 encoding, a hard per-call timeout, and (if Antigravity is included) stdin redirected to DEVNULL to avoid hanging on stdin
uses a tolerant JSON extractor for member output (raw parse, then ```json fences, then first {...} block) rather than assuming clean JSON
has the boss synthesize over anonymized/relabeled proposals (harness identity hidden) and falls back to a heuristic merge if the boss call itself fails

cases.prompt: council of claude and codex CLIs deliberating headlessly on the same prompt
expected_behavior: identifies this as the harness-implementation task (headless CLI council) rather than the API-only architecture or should-we-council decision
specifies the Claude Code invocation includes a disallowed-tools deny-list alongside bypassPermissions, framing every council member as read-only for deliberation
specifies Codex CLI is invoked via `codex exec` and that its JSONL event stream must be parsed for the final agent message rather than treated as plain stdout text
notes CLI flag lists are version-gated and should be re-verified against current official docs before relying on them

cases.prompt: one of my council members is a coding CLI and the whole run just hangs forever, never returns
expected_behavior: diagnoses likely causes: a one-shot CLI (e.g. Antigravity) waiting on stdin because it wasn't given stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, or a missing/insufficient per-call timeout
recommends start_new_session=True plus killing the whole process group (not just the child pid) on timeout, since coding harnesses spawn grandchildren that otherwise leak and keep billing
recommends a hard per-call timeout (order of a few minutes) and budget flags where the harness supports them so one wedged member cannot stall the council indefinitely
treats this as a subprocess-hygiene fix specific to LLM/agent harnesses, not a generic subprocess debugging question

cases.prompt: the boss model just returned a verdict that says 'decompose into subtasks' but only names one subtask, should we accept that as valid?
expected_behavior: flags that boss/synthesis output must be validated semantically, not just for syntactic JSON validity
specifically calls out rejecting a decomposition verdict that names fewer than two subtasks as an example of a semantic check
recommends falling back to a heuristic merge (e.g. picking the longest-rationale proposal) rather than accepting an invalid boss verdict or silently failing
recommends keeping every proposal, including failed ones, in the result object for provenance/audit even when the boss output needed correction
